subject: Opswell reserve sizing — slotting strategy and memory headroom
messages:

Subject: Initial telemetry + question on GPU mix for reserved capacity

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Initial telemetry + question on GPU mix for reserved capacity

Thanks Nora — quick read of the CSV looks useful. I summarized our recommended approach below and attached a short slotting sketch (proposed-slotting.pdf). TL;DR: pick a base reserve on A100 (for stable long-context memory) + a proportional H100 buffer for low-latency heavy-parallel inference; use L4 for cheap short-chat burst-offs.

Why this mix (short bullets):
- Memory headroom: your 8k-tail means model KV cache and activation memory matter. A100 (40GB/80GB flavors) gives predictable per-request memory footprint for long-context models we expect you'll run.
- Latency & concurrency: H100 offers higher sustained tensor throughput for large-batch parallelism (good for synchronous batch scoring during peaks) and is better when you want lower 99th percentile latency under contention.
- Cost & small-ops burst: L4 is far cheaper for short conversational calls — keep a small pool to offload <512-token sessions.

Slotting proposal (high level):
1) Reserve baseline: A100 pool sized for sustained steady-state concurrency (estimate: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent slots) to cover long-context inference without eviction.
2) Latency buffer: H100 buffer (2–4 cards) as a hot pool to absorb spikes and parallel batch queues; routing policy prefers H100 when latency SLO is strict and A100 pool is at >75% occupancy.
3) L4 burst band: small autoscale group for sub-512 token flows with fast spin-up + cache-awareness to avoid cold-KV penalties.
4) Memory padding: keep ~15% headroom on A100s for model growth and KV cache variability; avoid overpacking multi-tenant slots.

Open items for procurement and ops:
- Need your percent of requests that are >2k tokens (approx).
- Desired p99 latency SLO for conversational vs synthesis paths.
- Any compliance constraints for private deployment (if so, we should size private VPC differently).

I've cc'd Irene and Karthik for ops/quant guidance. If you want, we can run a short simulated slotting calc with your CSV to give token-per-dollar numbers.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-slotting.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

Adding operational color — quick notes we usually include when customers mix H100/A100/L4: 

- Preemption and packing: H100s can be utilized with tighter packing for high-throughput batchers; avoid using preemptible-only H100s for synchronous paths. For cost-sensitive bursts, preemptible L4 works well but plan for retries.
- Quantization & model variants: if you can run an int8 variant for synthesis, L4 can handle a noticeable share of work; otherwise A100 remains the safer baseline.
- KV cache fragmentation: long-context tails create variable KV sizes; when slotting, prefer fewer slots with reserved large memory (A100-80GB) over many smaller slots on 40GB to reduce eviction churn.
- Autoscaling policies: set scale-up aggressive on latency SLO misses, but conservative scale-down with a cooldown window to avoid oscillation during spiky loads.

I'll do a quick slot-level token-per-dollar sketch once you confirm the split of short vs long queries (Nora). Also, Connor: recommend we include a simple routing policy sample (region + model-variant fallback) in the final doc.

Irene Choi
Director, Inference Operations
Redwood Inference
